entities.summary: Humberto Ortega Saavedra was a Nicaraguan revolutionary, military leader, writer and businessman. One of the nine members of the National Directorate of the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN), he co-founded the Tercerista tendency faction within the FSLN and was the "major theorist" of the urban insurrection strategy that toppled the Somoza family dictatorship. A four-star general, Ortega was minister of defense from 1980 to 1995, between the victory of the Sandinista revolution in 1979 under the National Reconstruction Government, through the first presidency of his brother Daniel Ortega, and into the presidency of Violeta Chamorro who defeated Daniel Ortega in 1990.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a four-star general and key leader of the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN), Humberto Ortega played a crucial role in toppling the Somoza family dictatorship in Nicaragua, leading to significant regional implications for Central America and beyond. His influence on the FSLN's urban insurrection strategy had lasting effects on the region's politics and social movements.
